investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-29T11:24–11:31Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never produced any evidence, leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a full contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to run remote-agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is at the infrastructure scheduling layer rather than in the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definition. No evidence of a code regression is present; sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 129s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner never received a pod-ready signal, so no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the agent pod never starting.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 149s, zero evidence keys — confirms the same infrastructure constraint blocked a second independent pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 145s, zero evidence keys — confirms a third independent pod was also blocked.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=131871 (≈132s), which is within the warningLatencyMs threshold of 240000ms but the pod never became schedulable, so the check failed on unschedulability rather than latency.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1880-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the remote machine type is explicitly requested, meaning the pod must land on a kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
source-discovery.ranked-paths: suspectChanges is empty — no code change is identified as a regression hypothesis by source discovery.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 matching nodes (failed-check.message).

[Medium confidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is already constrained to only 2 nodes. If a node label was recently removed or the affinity rule was tightened, the effective capacity would drop further.

[Lower confidence] Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval probe runs plus any production workload, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling windows.

[Lower confidence] Leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883) holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes in the production cluster to confirm exhaustion. If confirmed, scale the node pool or free occupied VM slots before the next eval run.

Investigate why 4 of 6 cluster nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. If this is intentional, document the expected schedulable pool size. If it is due to label drift or a misconfiguration, restore the correct labels to expand the schedulable pool.

Review the withCleanup implementation in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure it reliably deletes remote-agent pods even when the eval probe fails mid-run, preventing VM slot leakage across eval cycles.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed ample remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause would not be resource exhaustion and another explanation (e.g., a quota admission webhook, a broken node resource plugin, or a pod spec error) would need to be investigated.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods was found to request a kata.peerpods.io/vm quantity of 0 or omit the resource entirely, the 'Insufficient' message would indicate a node-level plugin fault rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run immediately after this failure succeeded without any node scaling or pod cleanup, it would suggest the failure was a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' were found to also carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource with available capacity, it would indicate the node affinity rule is overly restrictive and is the primary constraint rather than resource exhaustion.

If no prior-run remote-agent pods were found occupying VM slots (i.e., withCleanup worked correctly), the leaked-pod hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would be pure capacity under-provisioning or external workload consumption.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes and fails with a WARN when capacity drops below a minimum threshold (e.g., 1 free slot), providing early warning before pod scheduling failures occur.
Add an eval check that verifies no orphaned or leaked remote-agent pods remain in the cluster after each eval cycle, catching withCleanup failures before they exhaust VM slot capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's nodeSelector/affinity is at or above a configured minimum, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to record the pod scheduling latency as a separate evidence field, enabling trend analysis that could surface capacity pressure before it becomes a full scheduling failure.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment on 2026-06-29 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. No preemption victims were available. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during this eval window was rejected by the scheduler (Unschedulable), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling evidence unreachable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm node pool; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production user impact.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval-triggered agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes carry, so even if VM slots were freed on other nodes, those nodes would still be ineligible. This is a configuration constraint that compounds the capacity problem.

Cluster autoscaler not triggering or not configured for the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful' indicate no scale-out occurred during the ~149s window, suggesting autoscaling is either absent, slow, or not enabled for this node type.

Concurrent eval runs or other workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if multiple eval runs or production workloads share the same 2-node VM pool, simultaneous scheduling pressure could exhaust capacity transiently.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was returned by any check, meaning the agent VM never became schedulable and the eval probe timed out before any runtime response could be collected.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were already at capacity, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the observability eval infrastructure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-29T11:24–11:31Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never produced any evidence, leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a full contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to run remote-agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is at the infrastructure scheduling layer rather than in the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definition. No evidence of a code regression is present; sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 129s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner never received a pod-ready signal, so no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the agent pod never starting.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 149s, zero evidence keys — confirms the same infrastructure constraint blocked a second independent pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 145s, zero evidence keys — confirms a third independent pod was also blocked.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=131871 (≈132s), which is within the warningLatencyMs threshold of 240000ms but the pod never became schedulable, so the check failed on unschedulability rather than latency.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1880-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the remote machine type is explicitly requested, meaning the pod must land on a kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
source-discovery.ranked-paths: suspectChanges is empty — no code change is identified as a regression hypothesis by source discovery.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 matching nodes (failed-check.message).

[Medium confidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is already constrained to only 2 nodes. If a node label was recently removed or the affinity rule was tightened, the effective capacity would drop further.

[Lower confidence] Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval probe runs plus any production workload, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling windows.

[Lower confidence] Leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883) holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

Review the withCleanup implementation in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure it reliably deletes remote-agent pods even when the eval probe fails mid-run, preventing VM slot leakage across eval cycles.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed ample remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause would not be resource exhaustion and another explanation (e.g., a quota admission webhook, a broken node resource plugin, or a pod spec error) would need to be investigated.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods was found to request a kata.peerpods.io/vm quantity of 0 or omit the resource entirely, the 'Insufficient' message would indicate a node-level plugin fault rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run immediately after this failure succeeded without any node scaling or pod cleanup, it would suggest the failure was a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' were found to also carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource with available capacity, it would indicate the node affinity rule is overly restrictive and is the primary constraint rather than resource exhaustion.

If no prior-run remote-agent pods were found occupying VM slots (i.e., withCleanup worked correctly), the leaked-pod hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would be pure capacity under-provisioning or external workload consumption.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes and fails with a WARN when capacity drops below a minimum threshold (e.g., 1 free slot), providing early warning before pod scheduling failures occur.
Add an eval check that verifies no orphaned or leaked remote-agent pods remain in the cluster after each eval cycle, catching withCleanup failures before they exhaust VM slot capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's nodeSelector/affinity is at or above a configured minimum, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to record the pod scheduling latency as a separate evidence field, enabling trend analysis that could surface capacity pressure before it becomes a full scheduling failure.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment on 2026-06-29 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. No preemption victims were available. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during this eval window was rejected by the scheduler (Unschedulable), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling evidence unreachable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm node pool; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production user impact.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval-triggered agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes carry, so even if VM slots were freed on other nodes, those nodes would still be ineligible. If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds (pod schedules and all 4 evidence keys are present), the failure was transient capacity pressure rather than a persistent exhaustion or misconfiguration.

If the eval runner itself had a credential or token failure that prevented createAgent from even submitting the pod, the scheduler message would not appear — the presence of the explicit Kubernetes Unschedulable message disproves a credential-layer failure, but this should be confirmed by checking runner logs.

If sibling checks for local agents (e.g., local-agent-create) also failed during the same window, the failure scope would extend beyond the remote-agent node pool, suggesting a broader infrastructure or API issue rather than kata.peerpods.io/vm-specific exhaustion.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was returned by any check, meaning the agent VM never became schedulable and the eval probe timed out before any runtime response could be collected.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were already at capacity, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the observability eval infrastructure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on both eligible nodes in the production-api cluster — no capacity available for a new remote agent pod at the time of the eval run (supported by all three sibling check messages)

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the remote-agent pod's node affinity or selector rules, meaning the schedulable node pool is structurally limited to exactly 2 nodes for this workload type, making the cluster sensitive to any concurrent VM usage

Tertiary: A concurrent workload or a previously created agent pod that was not cleaned up may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing the eval probe from acquiring capacity

Lower confidence: A node that previously provided kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have become unavailable (e.g., cordoned, drained, or failed), reducing the effective schedulable pool below what is needed for the eval

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and unused on the eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and returns all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), the exhaustion was transient and likely caused by a concurrent workload rather than a structural capacity deficit.
If the pod spec for remote agents does not request kata.peerpods.io/vm and the scheduler message was produced by a different resource constraint, the diagnosis would need to be revised.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are actually kata-capable nodes that were temporarily unavailable (e.g., cordoned), restoring them would disprove the structural two-node pool hypothesis.

If no other pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm at the time of the failure, the resource exhaustion may be caused by a node-level issue (e.g., the kata runtime reporting incorrect allocatable counts) rather than competing workloads.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and reports a distinct 'capacity-unavailable' status rather than a timeout failure.
Add an eval that tracks the count of active remote-agent pods in the cluster over time to detect capacity leaks from prior eval runs.
Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of kata-capable nodes are schedulable and not cordoned or drained, alerting when the eligible pool drops below a defined threshold.

Consider a sibling eval that verifies remote-agent pod cleanup (withCleanup) completes successfully after each probe run, to catch cases where eval teardown fails and leaves pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.
